lead: Sioux Falls is one of the fastest-growing cities in the Midwest, with many homes and basements built in recent decades. Hail, spring floods and tornadoes cause most of its water damage.
risk: hail and storm damage, basement water and river flooding
why: The Big Sioux River loops around Sioux Falls, and the city built a diversion channel in the 1960s to carry floodwater around it. Levees and the channel protect most neighborhoods, but heavy spring rain on frozen or soaked ground still sends water into low areas and basements. Most Sioux Falls homes have basements, and sump pumps work hard every spring.

Storms are the other big risk. On September 10, 2019, three tornadoes touched down in Sioux Falls overnight. They damaged homes and businesses across parts of the city, and roofs and windows were torn open in the rain. Hail is common almost every summer. Winters are cold and long, and pipes in outside walls and garages freeze in deep cold snaps.

image_caption: Hail and summer storms crack roofs across Sioux Falls.
problems: Homes across the city in spring
Low areas near the Big Sioux River
tips: Get the roof checked after any hail, even with no leak yet.
Test your sump pump before spring and add a battery backup.
Move snow away from the foundation before it melts.
Insulate pipes on outside walls before winter.
areas: Calls come from Downtown, Cathedral, McKennan Park, Pettigrew Heights, Whittier, All Saints and Sertoma, plus Brandon, Harrisburg and Tea.

faq.q: Does my Sioux Falls policy cover hail damage?
faq.a: Most home policies cover hail damage to the roof, siding and windows, plus rain that gets in through it. Many have a separate wind and hail deductible, sometimes a percentage of your home's value. Check yours before storm season so the claim is not a surprise.
